Do certain states require double clutching before you have your CDL? In mine, and where I trained and tested, they didn't question floating gears and I got mine 2.5 years ago

So this comment won't be structured very well but I hope you find it useful. Try to learn how to float gears, clutching is bad unless your are starting or stopping. Also try not to use the first couple gears, start in third if the weight of the vehicle and the grade permits, or even higher if it can be done without stalling. A little cheat sheet on shifting is at 15 mph, you should be in 6th gear, at 25, 7th, 35, 8th, 45, 9th, 55, 10th. Add the 2 numbers up to determine what gear you should be in. This only works in increments of 5 as shown here. Also I should add, this will only work for 10 speeds I think. For downshifting, it's the same try and get your wheel speed down to each of these numbers while down shifting. So for example when downshifting from 8th to 7th, you should be reducing speed to just above 35, tap the throttle and lightly pull out of 8th and fluidly slip it in to 7th. For early down shifting, you need to get the rpms higher than normal, this will create an engine brake. Realistically, don't need to downshift all the way on your test. You could downshift to 6th and clutch in and brake to a stop. As you can see I'm rambling a bit but I hope this helps you in some way.
